title: Nondemolition filtering of an embedded cluster-state scar under continuous local monitoring
authors: Ximo Wang, Xi Zhao, Xiayu Sun, Qiwei Han, Yuhang Wang, Chunxiao Du, Wenxiu Li, Hao Zhang, Rui Li
abstract: Identifying a low-entanglement eigenstate inside a many-body spectrum and preserving it during measurement are distinct tasks. We construct an explicit local ring Hamiltonian with an exact cluster-state eigenvector and study continuous monitoring of its stabilizer defects. For arbitrary mixed inputs, the conditional cluster fidelity is the initial target weight divided by the no-observed-click probability. A positive defect-operator gap gives finite-time bounds that hold for noncommuting Hamiltonian dynamics, nonnormal effective generators and imperfect detection. At fixed total monitoring rate, the guaranteed exponent falls inversely with system size; high conditional fidelity does not remove the preparation cost set by the initial overlap. Exact diagonalization up to eleven qubits gives finite-size evidence for a cluster-state outlier in a chaotic spectral background. Independent matrix and trajectory calculations verify the dynamics and a conservative coherent-error bound. This construction specializes established scar embedding and nondemolition verification frameworks, with explicit measurement assumptions, finite-time guarantees and resource limitations.
summary: This paper develops a method to protect a specific, low-entanglement quantum state (a cluster-state scar) embedded in a complex many-body system during continuous local measurement. By deriving rigorous bounds on the conditional cluster fidelity, the authors establish the fundamental limits on state preservation. The work is significant for quantum information theory as it provides a concrete, mathematically verified framework for measurement-assisted quantum control.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of nondemolition filtering—preserving a low-entanglement eigenstate (a 'scar') embedded in a complex many-body spectrum while undergoing continuous local measurement.
main_result: They provide a rigorous construction and finite-time bounds for the conditional cluster fidelity, showing that the preservation process is limited by the initial preparation overlap.
method: The analysis combines theoretical derivations of fidelity bounds using conditional probability and numerical diagonalization up to eleven qubits to provide finite-size evidence.
model_or_system: The system is an N-qubit ring governed by a local ring Hamiltonian, targeting an exact cluster-state eigenvector. The dynamics are modeled using a Lindblad generator incorporating continuous local monitoring.
key_observables: Conditional Cluster Fidelity ($F_C(t)$), No-observed-click probability ($S(t)$), and the initial overlap ($p$).
important_parameters: The monitoring rate ($\gamma$), system size ($N$), and the initial preparation overlap ($p$).
main_assumptions: The results rely on an explicit local embedding construction and are supported by formal verification (Lean 4); the evidence is limited to finite sizes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectrum showing the cluster eigenstate's position and the adjacent-gap ratio ($\langle r angle$), and time evolution plots comparing calculated fidelity/no-click probability against theoretical bounds.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by constructing the Hamiltonian, deriving the fidelity bounds, performing numerical diagonalization to show spectral evidence, and finally verifying the dynamics and bounds using formal proofs.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the fundamental problem of state preparation and preservation in noisy, open quantum systems, providing concrete, mathematically rigorous bounds for measurement-based quantum control.
